title: Melania Trump brokers humanitarian ceasefire for ravaged Ukraine city Oleshky
summary: Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will ‌begin on Oct. 29, the White House said on Friday.

image.caption: Demonstrators hold posters as they participate in a rally demanding the establishment of a humanitarian corridor to evacuate Ukrainian civilians from the town of Oleshky in Kherson region, on Oct. 6 in Kyiv, Ukraine. (Alina Smutko/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will ‌begin on Oct. 29, the White House said on Friday.
Ceasefire for Oleshky in southern Ukraine to begin late next week
Residents of the southern Ukrainian town, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported a deepening food crisis.

"Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in ​Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter ​and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway," a White House statement said.
The statement said Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with ​Russian and Ukrainian leadership ⁠to define the terms of the localized ceasefire.

"The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city ⁠on the brink of disaster. Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food and clean water," Melania Trump said in the statement.
The ceasefire ‌will allow non-military teams from both countries to visit residents in their homes and co-ordinate transportation for those wishing to evacuate to either Russia or Ukraine.
A still image taken from an undated drone video released Sept. 12 shows a destroyed buildings in Oleshky, Kherson region. (34th Separate Marine Brigade/Reuters)

The Kremlin said an evacuation in Oleshky would take at least a few days. It praised Melania Trump and said the undertaking was discussed in a recent call between her husband and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to the White House early last year, Melania Trump has been been active in trying to get Ukrainian children seized by Russia during the war returned to their families.

Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from Kherson, has a remaining population of 1,700 to ⁠2,000 people — primarily elderly residents, along with about 50 children — down from roughly 24,000 before ⁠the war, the White House said. About 90 per cent of the city was flooded ⁠following ⁠the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, ​according to the White House.
Starlink confusion

The development comes after a two-week period in which the White House's interventions into the nearly five-year war have received bracing criticism from Ukraine's European allies, Democrats and even some Republicans.

First, President Trump struck a deal with Putin to import diesel. The Trump administration has pressured Kyiv to halt its attacks on Russian energy infrastructure — which it blames for driving up the price of diesel.

Trump announced soon after, unilaterally, that the two sides had agreed to a ceasefire on energy attacks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was open to that possibility, but Russia had shown no inclination to halt its fire.

Zelenskyy on Oct. 14 then said Elon Musk's SpaceX had restricted its Starlink services. Throttling the speed of the satellite service, according to Ukraine officials, hampers its ability to conduct strikes on Russian targets and to defend itself from Russian drones using its own interceptor drones.

blocks.text: Trump and Musk, along with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, have since offered shifting explanations on precisely what occurred and who ordered the Starlink services throttled.
"Whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn't make any difference, I guess," Trump told reporters on Thursday. "The bottom line — [Musk] put it back."

The relationship between Trump and Zelenskyy has often been tense since 2019, when the U.S. president was impeached, though ultimately acquitted in the Senate, of pressuring the Ukraine president for political favours in exchange for military aid to Kyiv. Last year, Trump and Vice-President JD Vance berated Zelenskyy in the White House for what they perceived as a lack of gratitude for U.S. support of Ukraine.

In fighting on Friday, Moscow's largest airport, Sheremetyevo, resumed operations after it ‌was forced to briefly suspend its work and ask passengers to ​move to safe locations ​due to a Ukrainian drone threat.
Moscow Mayor Sergei ​Sobyanin said in a ⁠statement ⁠on Telegram that ‌air defence forces had shot down 21 Ukrainian drones that were headed to ⁠the Russian capital over a 2-hour period.

Rosaviatsiya, ⁠Russia's aviation watchdog, said ⁠earlier ⁠on Friday ​that three of Moscow's airports had ​temporarily ⁠suspended flight operations, something they do when there is Ukrainian drone activity.

The warring sides also engaged in one of their periodic exchanges of war prisoners, Ukraine officials confirmed on Friday, involving 270 people on each side being repatriated. Earlier in the week, the two sides exchanged the bodies of several people killed in the war, in Belarus.
More than 19,000 ‌Ukrainian civilians, including 762 ​children, have ​been killed since Russia launched ​its full-scale ⁠war, ⁠Ukraine's acting prosecutor general said ‌on Friday.
In 2026 alone, Ukrainian prosecutors ​confirmed ⁠the deaths ⁠of 2,960 ⁠civilians, ⁠including ​668 children, Anton ​Kovalskyi ⁠said on Telegram.
